result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers move the banner details into real text, rewrite the 'here' links, handle the chat widget's on-load attribute honestly and add phone fixes. A changes the working parts less: it keeps the inline onclick and avoids inventing a year. B replaces the onclick with addEventListener and adds a datetime with an assumed year, 2026. B does put the viewport tag directly in the head and honestly says it's unsure whether the vendor honours 'false'. Overall, A has the slight edge. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers move the banner details into real text, make the 'here' links descriptive, and add a viewport tag, a flexible image width and 44px tap targets. B leaves more of the working parts alone: it keeps the calendar button's inline onclick, while A rewrites it to addEventListener. B also avoids A's invented year in the time datetime and notes the details should come from booking data. A handles the chat widget more carefully, because it admits the vendor may ignore data-open-on-load="false", while B assumes that removing the attribute stops auto-open.
